What I pulled from the CSV (hand calc):

- 30% uplift on baseline -> target sustained capacity = ~44 A100s.
- Spike buffer to cover 90%-ile ~ +16 GPUs.

My working recommendation: commit to reserved 10 GPUs (to reduce unit cost) + maintain a managed on-demand burst buffer of ~16 GPUs during launch windows. This balances cost and risk. But I want infra to validate the p95 latency tradeoffs and whether we should instead reserve a slightly larger baseline and smaller burst to simplify billing.

Deliverables by EOD today: 1) validated GPU counts and cost delta, 2) proposed amendment language for procurement to add reserve + burst terms.

David / team — ran the numbers against the production telemetry: attaching a short summary. Key findings:
- Sustained load after uplift: ~43.8 A100-equivalent (matches your calc).
- To keep p95 latency <=45ms during 1–3h spikes we need an additional 14 GPUs if we keep current batching thresholds; with adaptive batch size + KV cache warmup we can reduce that to ~10 GPUs.
- Cost delta (monthly): reserving +10 GPUs (1yr term) lowers effective per-GPU/hr by ~28% vs on-demand burst. The burst pool (metered) for expected spike hours adds ~18% to monthly bill on our usage forecast.

Recommendation: commit to +10 reserved GPUs and enable a managed burst pool sized to 16 GPUs for the launch window, with automatic fallback to an alternate cheaper variant if burst exhausts. For procurement language, we should include a clause allowing temporary burst expansion for up to 8 weeks per year at metered rates.
